lesson.subtitle: Lesson 11 -- While I Was Paddling Out
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Renato | Lesson 11 -- While I Was Paddling Out
lesson.grammar_point: past continuous with past simple (when / while)

listenings.text: Good morning, everyone. One quick word before you go in. At about seven this morning a young surfer was paddling out on the north side when the sand moved under him and the rip took him eighty meters down the beach. He did the right thing. He was not panicking, he was not swimming against the water, he was just holding on to his board and waving one arm. We had him out in four minutes. So, two things for today. Do not surf the north corner on a falling tide, and if something goes wrong out there, stay with your board and shout.

The funny part is that I was having the best session of the month. Small, clean, nobody out. I was riding a wave into the shallow part, thinking about breakfast, honestly, when I heard this crack under my feet. I looked down and the board was in two pieces. And I was not even doing anything special. No air, no big turn, nothing. I was standing there going straight. My mate was filming from the beach and he got all of it, so now the whole club has seen me fall off a broken board in water up to my knees. He has not stopped sending it to people since Tuesday.

items.situation: Something went wrong in the water last month. Tell me, and start with the long action.
Somebody asks: "What were you doing at seven this morning?" Answer with two things.
Say what two other people were doing while you were surfing yesterday.
Name one thing that interrupted you yesterday. Use the two tenses in one sentence.
Ask three questions with "What were you doing when...?" to somebody you just met.
